articles.title: Rapture review – cult Spanish horror is a deeply strange cheese dream of cinemania
articles.summary: Pedro Almodóvar provides a vocal cameo and his style can be traced back to this influential film. This cult supernatural mystery from 1979 is a deeply strange cheese dream of a film from Spain, in which almost the entire opening 10 minutes unfolds in a jittery quiet.
body: At least some of its fascination stems from the marginal involvement of the young Pedro Almodóvar, who did voice-overdubbing for one female character. Director Iván Zulueta was to maintain his connection with Almodóvar from then on and much of Almodóvar’s procedure can be traced back to this influential film: the rapture for movies (what a character here calls “cinemania”), the double-stranded narrative, the queer euphoria and the importance of extended flashbacks.

The last time I saw Poncela on screen was in Juan Carlos Fresnadillo’s mysterious chiller Intact from 2001; there he played a man working for Max von Sydow’s casino owner, employed to use his mysterious gift for ill fortune to drain good luck away from gamblers enjoying winning streaks. He has the same haughty, doomy aura here.

articles.title: How Deep Is Your Love review – under the sea at Earth’s last frontier with the Psychedelic Elvis Worm
articles.summary: Film-maker Eleanor Mortimer accompanies a scientific expedition to the deep Pacific, where new creatures are abundant yet threatened by sea mining. For the marine biologists in this whimsical eco-documentary, the answer is about 5000 metres down.
body: Mortimer accompanies a team of scientists on an expedition to the eastern Pacific. It takes the ship’s robot four hours to descend the four kilometres to the ocean floor where it trundles along, grabber claw at the ready. A biologist explains that 80% of what they bring up to the surface is new to science. And one of the film’s pleasures is watching the wonderstruck awe on their faces as they clap eyes on never-before-seen creatures. The process of acquiring a Latin name for a new discovery can take years, so in the meantime scientists give them excellent temporary names like the Headless Chicken Monster and the Psychedelic Elvis Worm.

articles.title: Reanimated AI Greta Garbo stars again … in a ball-bearing advert
articles.summary: Relatives of Hollywood legend say her doppelganger could now be used for more glamorous roles. She shimmered in Hollywood’s silent movie era and lit up the first talkies – now Greta Garbo may be about to star in cinema’s new AI age.
body: More than a century after her screen debut and decades after her ashes were laid to rest in a Swedish woodland cemetery, the Hollywood superstar’s descendants are ready to consider an AI version of her taking a 21st-century film role.

Her likeness has already been reanimated for an advert for a Swedish industrial company, using AI generation technology. The practice some critics call “ghostploitation” has also been used in the case of the actor Val Kilmer, who died last year.

Asked if the AI Garbo could be cast in other roles, Craig Reisfield, one of three relatives who manage her legacy, told the Guardian: “I won’t say no, especially having seen what I’ve seen. It’s pretty incredible and lifelike. So what’s to say that you can’t bring Greta Garbo back in some kind of fashion in a film role?”

Reisfield said he was “flabbergasted” when he saw the AI version of his great-aunt created for publicity for the ball-bearings giant SKF. The connection comes because Garbo’s second-ever screen role was in a 1921 promotional film involving the Gothenburg-based company.
points: Relatives of Hollywood legend say her doppelganger could now be used for more glamorous roles.

articles.title: Beta Film Takes ‘Rex – Vienna Calling’ Worldwide as Season 2 Goes Into Production (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Beta Film has unveiled a broad international sales footprint for “Rex – Vienna Calling,” the latest incarnation of the three-decade-old “Rex – A Cop’s Best Friend” franchise, as production gets underway on a second season.
body: The deals come as the evergreen IP continues to find traction in an increasingly on-demand television market. Audience analytics firm PlumResearch describes mature streaming markets as shifting “from hits to habits,” with much viewing taking place across the long tail rather than being concentrated solely around new releases.

The longevity of “Rex” offers a case in point. Over its 30-year history, the police-dog franchise has spawned multiple local adaptations. Canadian remake “Hudson & Rex,” another long-running Beta title, was recently renewed for a tenth season.

“Rex – Vienna Calling” stars Maximilian Brückner (“War Horse,” “Cherry Blossoms”) as detective Max Steiner, who teams with German Shepherd Rex to tackle cases across Vienna. Six new feature-length episodes are currently shooting at some of the Austrian capital’s most recognizable locations.

articles.title: Zygi Kamasa’s U.K. Film Distributor True Brit Entertainment Files for Administration Due to ‘Extremely Challenging Market Conditions’
articles.summary: True Brit Entertainment, the U.K. theatrical distributor that launched less than three years ago, has filed for administration, a British legal process similar to Chapter 11 bankruptcy. The company, which was founded by former Lionsgate U.K.
body: True Brit was announced in Nov 2023 with a focus exclusively on U.K. films for theatrical release, launching with a stated aim to invest in and release 4-8 titles a year and co-finance over $50million worth of productions annually. The new venture came with funding led by talent management and entertainment company Three Six Zero, which reps names including Calvin Harris, Frank Ocean, FKA Twigs, plus a minority investment from Matthew Vaughn’s Marv.

The first True Brit release was “The Critic” starring Ian McKellen and Gemma Arterton, which it acquired out of Toronto in 2023 and put in U.K. cinemas the following year. This was followed by the Danny Dyer comedy “Marching Powder,” which hit a high note, grossing more than $4 million in the U.K. and Ireland. But subsequent releases, including Gurinder Chadha’s musical comedy-drama “Christmas Karma” and the boxing drama “Giant,” both of which True Brit co-produced, struggled, as did “The Death of Robin Hood,” which earned under $800,000.
points: True Brit Entertainment, the U.K. theatrical distributor that launched less than three years ago, has filed for administration, a British legal process similar to Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

articles.title: Amazon MGM Execs Javiera Balmaceda, Nicole Morganti Talk Big Spanish-Language Action Swings, the Push for Scale at Iberseries & Platino Industria
articles.summary: Speaking at the Iberseries & Platino Industria conference in Madrid, Amazon MGM execs Javiera Balmaceda and Nicole Morganti offered a candid look at how the streamer decides which non-English language projects to back, pointing to “Zeta” in Spain and “Venganza” in Mexico as examples of taking…
body: Morganti said “Zeta,” an espionage actioner starring Mario Casas and produced by Pablo Isla’s Fonte Films, was a chance to prove that Spain could deliver a big action movie with a distinctly Spanish identity. “Spain has a strong ability to make action,” she said, noting that the film also benefited from its mix of action, family and emotion. The movie ranked among Amazon Prime Video most watched Global Top Ten hits earlier this year.

Balmaceda, head of international originals, Latin America, Canada and Australia for Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios, described “Venganza” as a similar bet for Mexico. The challenge was convincing Amazon that a Mexican production could deliver the scale and action audiences expect from the genre.
“We believed a Mexican production could tell a story that would resonate globally and demonstrate that great action could come from somewhere other than Hollywood,” she said.

Neither project was an automatic greenlight. Morganti said the teams had to make the case around directors, talent and production capabilities. “You have to keep pushing and show the different elements of why the project could work,” she said.

body: US actor Chad Lowe and his wife, producer Kim Painter, have said they are "deeply heartbroken" following the death of their "beloved" 13-year-old daughter Fiona.
"She was a loving young girl who was smart, creative and loved to dance," the family said in a statement to Page Six, external and People, external.
"She was adored by her sisters and she was deeply loved by her parents. In fact, she was the light of our lives.

articles.title: SKF advert review – let’s hope this dull AI Greta Garbo is not the future
articles.summary: Swedish-American actor exhumed for bizarre, humourless 99 seconds that give us another reason to resent AI. Poor Greta Garbo. Perhaps, in life, she thought her final indignity would be the Peter Cook and Dudley Moore TV sketch from 1970, showing Pete as the legendary recluse standing on the back of…
body: The AI Greta Garbo is a bizarre soignée figure, a Stepford robo-star, a Hallmark-greeting-card parody of the icy hauteur, distraite sensuality and deadpan comedy that Garbo projected in life. The AI Garbo is like the classiest ever presenter of a TV shopping channel, purring her way through a dull and humourless script that seeks to create a brand synergy between the frictionless ball-bearings manufactured by SKF and what the company imagines to be Garbo’s own all-important smoothness. But Garbo’s impact rested on something other than smoothness. “One of my first films was for SKF and now I’m back for my last,” AI Greta remarks.
Let’s hope this dull AI Garbo is not the way of the future. Guardrails were never more badly needed.

articles.title: Massive Studios, ‘Garfield Movie’ Writers and Producer Todd Garner Team on AI Animated Short Films
articles.summary: Massive co-founder Reza Sixo Safai, scribes Paul A. Kaplan and Mark Torgove and Garner detailed the projects and their process during a panel at the Toronto International Film Festival.
body: A trio of animated shorts set around the Christmas holiday and powered by artificial intelligence is in the works and poised to debut before the end of the year — for free.

Safai, a co-founder at Massive Studios — a firm described as a “filmmaker-led” studio that develops film, TV, animation and branded entertainment using AI tools alongside traditional filmmaking ones — will direct the shorts from scripts by Kaplan and Torgove with Garner handling producing duties.

They provided a timeline, too: a trailer will debut Thanksgiving weekend in November, and the final films will be made available free of charge on Christmas Eve. There are some details yet to be announced like a streaming or distribution partner and some creative elements like titles, voice cast, creative collaborators and more.

That said, in statements provided to The Hollywood Reporter, the collaborators insist that the short films are creative-led animated projects that began as hand-drawn designs created by artists. The works will be combined with actor performances to establish the characters’ “proportions, expressions, costumes, textures and personalities before the technology is used to help bring them into motion.”

articles.title: Can Drama Change the World? Creators of Series on Far-Right Politics, Climate Crisis and More Weigh in
articles.summary: Creatives behind the likes of 'Borgen,' 'The Best Immigrant,' eco-thriller 'After Us,' sexual aggression drama 'Pubertat,' and historical HIV drama 'Henki' shared their motivations and goals at Iberseries.
body: The panelists were Danish Borgen and Follow the Money writer Jeppe Gjervig Gram, Belgian writer Cristina Poppe ( The Best Immigrant ), Norwegian writer and Scanbox Production development producer Jan Trygve Røyneland, French creator Louis Aubert ( After Us ), and Spanish director, screenwriter and actress Leticia Dolera ( Pubertat – Secrets, Lies, and Human Castles ).

Gram lauded Danish public broadcaster DR for being up for pushing the envelope with Borgen. After the financial crisis, Follow the Money made sense to him, and again, DR came through for him. “Nobody had done a show about Big Finance, and DR was brave enough,” he said.
And he emphasized that while his shows may be dark, “I always want audiences to leave on a hopeful note.”
